title: Orchard and Postcard
premise: Sebastian Delacroix, a lighthouse keeper's granddaughter who writes romance novels but refuses to live one, hires a charming stranger to pose as her partner at the Delacroix family reunion on Gullwing Island. The stranger, Elias Marsh, turns out to be the developer whose company is quietly buying out the island's bakery row — including the lease that keeps Sebastian's late grandmother's bakery alive. As their fake courtship deepens into something real, Sebastian must choose between protecting her family's loyalty and exposing the truth about Elias's employer, while Elias must decide whether his career is worth the woman who taught him what home means. In the end, Elias testifies against his own company, Sebastian signs a new lease with money she almost refuses, and they open the bakery together — love finally in the present tense.
about_author: Wren Whitlock grew up above a failing bakery on a windswept Atlantic island, where she learned that love stories are mostly about leases, inheritances, and the courage to stay. She now writes from a converted boathouse, where every draft smells faintly of salt and burnt sugar.

chapters.title: The Rehearsed Sentence
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Ten years after swearing off love, Sebastian drafts the same opening line of her novel for the hundredth time while the bakery's eviction notice sits unopened on the counter. Emotional beat: quiet dread disguised as routine.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Ferry Dock
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Rushing to catch the mainland ferry for supplies, she collides with Elias Marsh, a polished outsider asking oddly specific questions about island property. They bicker; he buys her coffee as an apology. Beat: reluctant spark.

chapters.title: The Invitation Nobody Wanted
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Her mother calls: the full Delacroix reunion, three days, everyone expecting news of Sebastian's 'mystery partner' since a cousin's wedding rumor spiraled. Panicked, Sebastian remembers the ferry stranger. Beat: desperation dressed as scheming.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Sebastian finds him at the island inn and proposes a paid fake relationship. Elias, secretly scouting the bakery block for his firm, agrees — telling himself it's convenient cover. Beat: complicity with a hidden cost.

chapters.title: Arrivals
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The reunion begins at the family orchard house; Elias charms aunts, deflects uncles, and memorizes details about the bakery that make Sebastian uneasy. Beat: performance so good it starts to feel like trespass.

chapters.title: Dessert
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. At the reunion dinner, under string lights and her grandmother's recipes, the fake date stops feeling fake — a shared laugh over burnt cobbler lands somewhere real. Elias's hand trembles when it brushes hers. Beat: the mask slips.

chapters.title: What Elias Knew First
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Alone at night, Elias reviews the acquisition file: Delacroix Bakery, flagged for demolition phase two. He realizes he's fallen for the woman whose livelihood he's erasing — and says nothing. Beat: guilt taking root.

chapters.title: Orchard Walks
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Morning walks through the abandoned family orchard become ritual; Sebastian tells him about her grandfather's lighthouse, Elias invents nothing for once. A near-kiss is interrupted by a cousin. Beat: tenderness outrunning the lie.

chapters.title: The Lease Runs Out
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The formal notice arrives: sixty days. Sebastian's mother urges selling; Sebastian refuses to let go of the last thing her grandmother left. She and Elias fight about legacy versus pragmatism. Beat: first true fracture.

chapters.title: Company Man
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. His boss arrives on-island, pressuring Elias to close the deal fast and mocking his 'distraction.' Elias requests the bakery be moved to phase three — a small rebellion with a deadline. Beat: loyalty beginning to tilt.

chapters.title: Postcards from Nowhere
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sorting her grandmother's things, Sebastian finds unsent postcards addressed to a man in the city — evidence of a secret, sacrificed love. She reads them aloud to Elias; both recognize themselves. Beat: history rhyming.

chapters.title: The Almost
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Rainstorm, power outage, one candle in the bakery kitchen. Elias nearly confesses everything twice; instead he kisses her, and she kisses back, and the truth curdles under it. Beat: intimacy built on a fault line.

chapters.title: Phase Two
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Surveyors stake the orchard and bakery block overnight. Sebastian discovers the acquisition documents — with Elias's signature on the initial assessment. Beat: the floor giving way.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Lighthouse
chapters.summary: Both POVs. At the ruined lighthouse, Sebastian demands the truth; Elias gives it, all of it, and offers to fix it. She sends him away: 'You rehearsed your sentence too, and you still didn't say it.' Beat: heartbreak with dignity.

chapters.title: Ten Days of Silence
chapters.summary: Split POVs. Sebastian throws herself into a legal appeal with the islanders; Elias drafts a resignation letter he can't send. Both reread the postcards / the assessment file nightly. Beat: parallel ache.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The zoning hearing goes badly; the company's lawyers are ruthless, and Sebastian's testimony falters — until a familiar figure enters the room. Beat: hope arriving sideways.

chapters.title: For the Record
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias takes the stand against his own employer, revealing falsified environmental assessments and the scheme to force sales. He torches his career in eleven minutes. Beat: the rehearsed sentence, finally spoken — as testimony.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The acquisition collapses; the island wins, but Elias vanishes before she can find him. Her mother, softened by the postcards, admits her own regret. Beat: victory hollowed by absence.

chapters.title: The Last Postcard
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A postcard arrives — no return address, only the lighthouse coordinates and a date. Sebastian wrestles with pride, then with fear, then boards the ferry with a tin of cobbler. Beat: choosing vulnerability.

chapters.title: Boathouse
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Unemployed and staying in Wren Whitlock's rented boathouse through an old college favor, Elias has written her a letter a day and sent none. She appears at his door. Beat: reckoning without armor.

chapters.title: Present Tense
chapters.summary: Both POVs. On the dock, Sebastian says the sentence she's rehearsed for a decade — not the novel's opening line, but 'I choose this, and I choose you.' Elias answers with the letter stack. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: Orchard and Postcard
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Sebastian's POV. One year later: the bakery reopens with Elias's name on the lease beside hers, the orchard replanted, the postcards framed behind the register. The novel's final line writes itself. Beat: home, earned.
